units.t: Notation Basics: Staff, Clefs and Pitch

learn: Music is notated on a five-line staff; the grand staff joins treble and bass clefs with a brace.
The treble (G) clef curls around G above middle C; the bass (F) clef's dots surround F below middle C.
The alto (C) clef, used by violas, centres on middle C.
check: The treble clef is also called the ___ clef.
The alto clef is used by...
lessons.try: Write middle C in treble, bass and alto clefs.

learn: Pitches repeat in octaves; scientific pitch notation names middle C as C4.
A4 vibrates at 440 Hz, the standard tuning pitch.
Each octave up doubles the frequency.
lessons.try: Find C3, C4 and C5 on a keyboard.

learn: Sharps raise a half step, flats lower, naturals cancel; double sharps and double flats move two half steps.
Enharmonic equivalents sound the same: F♯ and G♭.
Accidentals apply for the rest of the measure.
check: A double sharp raises a note...
lessons.try: Write five enharmonic pairs.

learn: Whole, half, quarter, eighth, sixteenth and thirty-second notes each halve the one before.
Dots add half the value; ties join values.
Rests have matching values.
lessons.try: Write and clap a four-bar rhythm with dotted notes and rests.

learn: Simple meters divide beats in two (2/4, 3/4, 4/4); compound meters divide in three (6/8, 9/8, 12/8).
Duple, triple and quadruple describe beats per measure.
6/8 is compound duple: two beats each divided in three.
lessons.try: Conduct patterns for 2/4, 3/4, 4/4 and 6/8.

learn: Count simple meter "1 e & a"; compound meter "1 la li 2 la li".
Counting aloud builds accurate rhythm.
Syncopation and triplets need careful counting.
check: A triplet fits three notes in the time of...
lessons.try: Count and clap a syncopated line aloud.

learn: Major scale pattern: W W H W W W H.
Scale degrees have names: tonic, supertonic, mediant, subdominant, dominant, submediant, leading tone.
The leading tone pulls strongly to the tonic.
check: The fifth scale degree is the...
W W H W W W H
W H W W H W W
H W W W H W W
lessons.try: Build major scales on D, E♭ and A.

lessons.t: Key Signatures and the Circle of Fifths
learn: The circle of fifths arranges keys by adding one sharp or flat at each step.
Order of sharps: F C G D A E B. Order of flats: B E A D G C F.
The last sharp is the leading tone; the second-to-last flat names the key.
check: The key with three sharps is...
The key with two flats is...
lessons.try: Draw the circle of fifths with all major keys.

learn: Transposing moves music to a different key while keeping intervals.
Singers transpose to fit their range.
Some instruments (clarinet in B♭, French horn in F) read transposed parts.
check: A B♭ clarinet is a ___ instrument.
lessons.try: Transpose a melody from C major to G major.

learn: Natural minor: W H W W H W W.
Harmonic minor raises the seventh, creating a leading tone.
Melodic minor raises the sixth and seventh ascending and lowers them descending.
lessons.try: Play A natural, harmonic and melodic minor.

learn: Relative keys share a key signature (C major and A minor).
Parallel keys share a tonic (C major and C minor).
Composers modulate between related keys for contrast.
check: The relative minor of F major is...
The parallel minor of G major is...
Changing key within a piece is...
lessons.try: Find the relative and parallel minor of G major.

learn: Modes are scales built on different degrees of the major scale.
Ionian (major), Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Aeolian (natural minor), Locrian.
Dorian is common in folk and jazz; Mixolydian in rock and Celtic music.
check: D to D on white keys is...
lessons.try: Play D Dorian on the white keys and describe its sound.

learn: Count letter names inclusively: C to F is a fourth.
Simple intervals are within an octave; compound intervals are larger (a ninth is an octave plus a second).
Melodic intervals are sequential; harmonic intervals sound together.
check: A ninth is an octave plus a...
Notes sounding together form a ___ interval.
lessons.try: Name ten intervals by number.

learn: Perfect: unison, fourth, fifth, octave. Major/minor: second, third, sixth, seventh.
Augmented intervals are a half step larger than perfect or major; diminished are smaller than perfect or minor.
The tritone (augmented fourth or diminished fifth) spans six half steps.
check: C to E is a ___ third.
C to E♭ is a ___ third.
lessons.try: Build major and minor thirds on five notes.

learn: Link intervals to familiar songs to recognise them by ear.
Perfect fifths sound open; minor seconds sound tense.
Interval inversion: a third inverts to a sixth; major becomes minor.
check: A major third inverts to a...
lessons.try: Identify ten intervals by ear.

learn: Major triad: major third + minor third (C-E-G).
Minor: minor third + major third (A-C-E). Diminished: two minor thirds (B-D-F). Augmented: two major thirds (C-E-G♯).
In a major key, I, IV and V are major; ii, iii and vi minor; vii° diminished.
check: In a major key, ii is...
lessons.try: Build all four triad qualities on D.

learn: Root position has the root in the bass; first inversion has the third; second inversion has the fifth.
Figured bass numbers (6, 6/4) indicate inversions.
Inversions create smoother bass lines.
check: First inversion has the ___ in the bass.
Second inversion has the ___ in the bass.
lessons.try: Write C major in all three positions.

learn: Seventh chords add a seventh above the root.
Types: major seventh (Cmaj7), dominant seventh (G7), minor seventh (Am7), half-diminished (Bø7).
The dominant seventh (V7) strongly resolves to I.
lessons.try: Play and compare four types of seventh chord.

learn: Tonic (I, vi) is home; predominant (ii, IV) leads away; dominant (V, vii°) creates tension that resolves to tonic.
The basic progression is T-PD-D-T.
ii-V-I is the most common progression in jazz.
lessons.try: Write four progressions following T-PD-D-T.

learn: Authentic (V-I), plagal (IV-I), half (ending on V) and deceptive (V-vi).
A perfect authentic cadence has both chords in root position and the tonic in the melody.
Deceptive cadences surprise the listener.
lessons.try: Find cadences in a hymn or folk song.

learn: In four-part writing (soprano, alto, tenor, bass), move voices smoothly by step.
Avoid parallel fifths and octaves between voices.
Resolve the leading tone up to the tonic.
check: Four-part writing uses SATB: soprano, alto, tenor and...
lessons.try: Harmonise a simple melody in four parts.

learn: Movable-do solfège: do re mi fa sol la ti do.
In minor (la-based), the tonic is la.
Solfège builds pitch memory and sight-singing.
check: In movable do, the tonic of major is...
lessons.try: Sing a major scale and simple melodies in solfège.

learn: Melodic dictation: hear a melody and write it down.
Listen for contour, rhythm, then specific pitches.
Rhythmic dictation trains rhythmic memory.
lessons.try: Take dictation of a four-bar melody.

learn: Before playing, check key, time signature, tempo and tricky spots.
Keep a steady beat; don't stop for mistakes.
Read ahead by looking a beat or more beyond what you're playing.
lessons.try: Sight-read a new piece using the strategy.

learn: Balanced posture reduces tension for singers and instrumentalists.
Diaphragmatic breathing supports tone.
Release jaw, shoulder and hand tension.
lessons.try: Practise breathing exercises before playing.

learn: Musicians can develop overuse injuries; take breaks every 20-30 minutes.
Warm up physically and musically.
Protect hearing with earplugs in loud ensembles.
lessons.try: Plan a practice session with warm-ups and breaks.

learn: Set specific goals for each session.
Slow practice and repetition build accuracy.
Record yourself and listen critically.
lessons.try: Keep a practice journal for two weeks.

learn: Ensemble players balance, blend and match intonation.
Follow the conductor's gestures for tempo, dynamics and cues.
Listen across the group, not just to yourself.
lessons.try: Rehearse a piece focusing on balance.

learn: Arrive prepared with music, pencil and instrument.
Mark parts with pencil; stop playing when the conductor stops.
Respect others' time and efforts.
lessons.try: Write a rehearsal etiquette checklist.

learn: Stage presence includes walking on confidently, bowing and staying focused.
Recover from mistakes without showing them.
Reflect afterward on what went well and what to improve.
lessons.try: Perform with an ensemble and write a reflection.
